edgeCutoff.twin: The short interval cutoff is the product of two smooth transition ramps of width epsilon times x to power theta. It is the permitted choice of g, transported to the lopsided interval.
edgeCutoff.instance: x one, theta one, epsilon one quarter and t one give a point strictly inside the constant one region.

edgeCutoff_nonneg.twin: The chosen cutoff is nonnegative for every real input.
edgeCutoff_nonneg.instance: x one, theta one, epsilon one quarter and t one give cutoff one.

edgeCutoff_le_one.twin: The chosen cutoff is at most one for every real input.

one_sub_edgeCutoff_eq_zero_of_inner.twin: For positive ramp width, one minus the cutoff vanishes at points at least that width from each endpoint.

edge_count_bound.twin: For positive theta and epsilon strictly between zero and one, all sufficiently large x have W times the norm of the edge character sum in every wheel class at most eight epsilon x to power theta. This counts unweighted edges and asserts no weighted sieve estimate.
edge_count_bound.instance: theta three fifths and epsilon one quarter satisfy the parameter hypotheses. Class one modulo W is permitted at every sufficiently large x.
edge_count_bound.next: Next verify the finite unsmoothing inequality.

unsmoothing_norm_bound.twin: For nonnegative coefficients and a cutoff at most one, the unsmoothed Fourier error is at most the smoothed error plus the nonnegative weighted edge mass plus the absolute mean times the unweighted edge Fourier norm. All phases have norm one.
unsmoothing_norm_bound.instance: s containing one, coefficient two, cutoff one half, phase one and mean two give zero error with a nonzero weighted edge mass one.
unsmoothing_norm_bound.next: Next verify smoothness and support of the cutoff.

hyp1_of_unsmoothing_estimates704.twin: For positive theta, any nonnegative coefficient family and real mean function satisfy eventual Hyp1 if supplied with a smoothed Fourier estimate for every positive cutoff width below one, a weighted edge bound with one constant uniform in the width, and an eventual absolute mean bound. The three analytic inputs remain explicit hypotheses. This is the generic unsmoothing implication and supplies no estimate for the actual Harman coefficients.
hyp1_of_unsmoothing_estimates704.instance: The identically zero coefficient family and mean satisfy all three hypotheses with edge constant zero and mean bound zero. Choosing every smoothed threshold at least two makes its nonnegative error budget well defined. The finite unsmoothing lemma also has a nonzero one index model.

This reuses the lab AP Selberg proof and its Apache 2.0 port.

No prime distribution or reference mean hypothesis is used.

The estimate is uniform over coprime numerators and denominators with denominator at least log x to power five A and at most Q. It assumes absolute q gamma minus a below one over Q.
